## Enabled skills are binding

The Skill Vault has installed the skills below into `.claude/skills`. They are
house rules, not suggestions: consult the ones that bear on the work
**before** starting it, rather than when a description happens to
catch your eye.

- **blendporter-expert** (`.claude/skills/blendporter-expert/SKILL.md`) — Expert for the BlendPorter Godot editor plugin (addons/blendporter/) in the godototype repo. Use this skill whenever adding settings, extending the import pipeline, debugging import behaviour, or understanding how project-level defaults and per-file import options interact.
- **camera-expert** (`.claude/skills/camera-expert/SKILL.md`) — Expert for the godototype camera system (camera/). Use this skill whenever working on camera modes, the priority/blend claim stack, the CameraManager singleton, VirtualCamera rig behaviour, mouse-look/orbit/free-fly controls, or the `camera` console command. Activate automatically when the user mentions the camera, a camera mode (follow/fixed/orbit/chase/freefly), camera framing/aiming, mouse-look, camera blending, or a CameraClaim.
- **euphoria-expert** (`.claude/skills/euphoria-expert/SKILL.md`) — Euphoria/NaturalMotion ragdoll physics expert for the godototype repo (assets/ragdoll/). Use this skill EVERY TIME you examine ragdoll debug logs, analyze locomotion behaviour, or discuss balance/stepping/posture controller logic. This skill is mandatory whenever the user pastes log output from RagdollDebugOverlay, FootStepper, BalanceController, SpinePostureController, or StanceController — do not wait to be asked. It defines the Euphoria reference patterns that all controller logic must follow, the deviation classification process, and how discovered deviations get split into board cards.
- **event-expert** (`.claude/skills/event-expert/SKILL.md`) — Expert for the godototype composable event system (formerly "effect"). Use this skill whenever designing, extending, or debugging the event system (events/) or any consumer of it (powerups, traps, pickups, magnets, etc.). Activate automatically when the user asks about adding a new EventType, EventTrigger, EventTarget, or any design question about the event layer separation.
- **kaizend-expert** (`.claude/skills/kaizend-expert/SKILL.md`) — Expert for the kaizend monorepo: the orchestrator's passes (Work, Unblock, garbage time, PR flow), the wind-down engine, post-completion obligations, how to add a pass, and the surrounding structure — the plugin split, Projects/Areas, card attribution, and the Skill Vault. Activate whenever working anywhere in ~/repo/kaizend (packages/kaizend-server, kaizend-app, kaizend-shared, kaizend-plugin-api, packages/plugins/*), touching board.yaml / projects.yaml / app.yaml, or reasoning about what the runner picks up and why.
- **pluginlogger-expert** (`.claude/skills/pluginlogger-expert/SKILL.md`) — Expert for the godototype PluginLogger system (addons/plugin_logger/) — the single structured logging channel for all game code in that repo, including per-instance DiagChannel output, the CustomGroups.json group/level model, and the GlobalInterceptor capture hook. Activate whenever adding or retuning a log group, adding diagnostic output to a component, debugging missing/flooding log lines, or working in addons/plugin_logger/.
- **session-accounting** (`.claude/skills/session-accounting/SKILL.md`) — How a terminal session leaves its bill on the story it worked: register the card with terminal-cost.py at the start, book the spend (tokens, turns, duration, cost) into the story's journal and the board's costs.jsonl at every checkpoint, and let the SessionEnd hook catch whatever is left. Proactive by contract — the user closes the window when the work is done and never asks for this. Applies to every terminal session that works a kaizend board card.
- **skill-refinement** (`.claude/skills/skill-refinement/SKILL.md`) — Audits the shop's prose against the tree after a change lands: every enabled vault skill, the generated CLAUDE.md mandate block in each sync target, and docs/*.md in the repo touched. Verifies each named symbol (route, path, knob, area, epic, tag) against the code and /v1/app-config before believing the prose, and edits skills through PUT /v1/skills/{id} rather than the synced .claude/skills copy. Use it after any rename/removal, when a numbered plan's last step lands, or when a card shows up with a dead tag or an epic name in area:.
- **skill-router** (`.claude/skills/skill-router/SKILL.md`) — The index of this vault: what each enabled skill covers and which repo it belongs to. Read it when you have a task in hand and want to know which domain skill owns it — especially when the task spans two subsystems, or when you are in a repo whose skills you haven't used before. Not a trigger skill; it routes, it does not do work.
- **story-discipline** (`.claude/skills/story-discipline/SKILL.md`) — How this shop turns a request into work: every task the user gives you becomes a board card BEFORE the work starts, written with title/area/tags and always both context: and effort:, created through POST /v1/boards/{board}/cards with your own X-Kaizend-Context header, and edited through the API rather than the file on disk. Also covers the way out: every card a session works lands in a column and carries a ## Handoff log entry before you report back. A card whose done-line came true goes to 05_TESTING/06_DONE; one that did not has exactly three exits, and you pick it, never the user — (1) the rest of the work lives in other cards, so depends_on them and back to 01_TODO; (2) 08_FAILED with a concrete retry plan a fresh context can run; (3) it truly cannot be done or only the user can decide, so tell them the real reason (08_FAILED or 03_STUCK with question-shaped blockers). Never close an unmet card as 'answered' or 'premise refuted', and never hand the column choice back. A finding that names work becomes its own card, and an unmeetable acceptance criterion is itself a finding to file. Not a keyword skill — it applies to every task, in every repo.
